statement: Define Common(L) to mean: 0 <= L <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)) and there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i <= len(nums1)-L, 0 <= j <= len(nums2)-L, and for every k with 0 <= k < L, nums1[i+k] = nums2[j+k]. Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r is the maximum L such that Common(L); equivalently, Common(r) holds and for every L with r < L <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)), Common(L) is false.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: For every nums1 and nums2 satisfying the preconditions, find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, access out of bounds, or panic.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, 0 <= r <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)).
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Define Common(L) to mean: 0 <= L <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)) and there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i <= len(nums1)-L, 0 <= j <= len(nums2)-L, and for every k with 0 <= k < L, nums1[i+k] = nums2[j+k]. Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, Common(r) holds; that is, there is an actual common contiguous subarray of length r.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Define Common(L) to mean: 0 <= L <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)) and there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i <= len(nums1)-L, 0 <= j <= len(nums2)-L, and for every k with 0 <= k < L, nums1[i+k] = nums2[j+k]. Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, for every L with r < L <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)), Common(L) is false; no longer common contiguous subarray exists.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) and every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), nums1[i] != nums2[j].
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r: if len(nums1) <= len(nums2), then r = len(nums1) if and only if there exists j with 0 <= j <= len(nums2)-len(nums1) and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), nums1[i] = nums2[j+i]; and if len(nums2) <= len(nums1), then r = len(nums2) if and only if there exists i with 0 <= i <= len(nums1)-len(nums2) and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), nums2[j] = nums1[i+j].
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r1 and find_length(nums2, nums1) returns a result r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Let rev(x) denote the array with len(rev(x)) = len(x) and rev(x)[i] = x[len(x)-1-i] for every 0 <= i < len(x). Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r and find_length(rev(nums1), rev(nums2)) returns a result r', r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: For every array a satisfying the same length/value constraints as nums1 (1 <= len(a) <= 1000 and 0 <= a[i] <= 100 for every i) and such that nums1 is a prefix of a (len(nums1) <= len(a) and nums1[i] = a[i] for every 0 <= i < len(nums1)), whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r and find_length(a, nums2) returns a result r', we have r' >= r.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: For every integer c such that the arrays a and b defined by a[i] = nums1[i] + c for 0 <= i < len(nums1) and b[j] = nums2[j] + c for 0 <= j < len(nums2) still satisfy the same length/value constraints (0 <= a[i] <= 100 and 0 <= b[j] <= 100), whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r and find_length(a, b) returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums1) >= 1, len(nums2) >= 1, len(nums1) <= 1000, len(nums2) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 100, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 100.

statement: Define Common(L) to mean: 0 <= L <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)) and there exist indices i, j with 0 <= i <= len(nums1)-L, 0 <= j <= len(nums2)-L, and for every k with 0 <= k < L, nums1[i+k] = nums2[j+k]. Whenever find_length(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, for every L with 0 <= L <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)), Common(L) holds if and only if L <= r.
